title: Vicky Kaushal Has Blocked Eighteen Months of His Life for One Film. He Will Play Parashurama. Shraddha Kapoor May Join Him.
excerpt: The actor will undergo six months of physical transformation before a year of exclusive filming for Mahavatar — the most intensive commitment any Bollywood star has made to a single project in 2026.
body:
There is a version of Bollywood where actors juggle four films a year, promote each one for a week, and move on. **Vicky Kaushal** has decided he wants no part of it.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=2xgITictQXY</youtube>

The actor has blocked eighteen consecutive months — from June 2026 through December 2027 — exclusively for **Mahavatar**, the mythological epic from **Maddock Films** in which he will play **Chiranjeevi Parashurama**, the immortal warrior-sage of Hindu tradition. During that window, he will not take on any other project. No brand shoots squeezed in between schedules. No announcement teasers for the next thing. Just Parashurama.

The commitment begins immediately after Kaushal wraps **Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Love and War**, the prestige drama also starring **Ranbir Kapoor** and **Alia Bhatt**. Bhansali is pushing through a crucial 50-day schedule that started in May, with the aim of wrapping by end of June. The moment cameras stop rolling on that set, Kaushal transitions straight into a six-month preparatory phase for Mahavatar.

> "The prep is going on for 6-7 months. We have worked on the set design, weapon design, how every character would look. The scripting is done. Yet, we need more time." — Amar Kaushik

Director **Amar Kaushik** — the man behind **Stree** and **Stree 2**, two of the most commercially dominant Hindi films in recent memory — has designed a training module that goes well beyond the usual gym-and-diet regimen. The programme encompasses a rigorous physical transformation to bulk Kaushal's frame to mythological proportions, alongside acting workshops focused on the psychological and spiritual depth of Parashurama. This is a character who taught **Bheeshma, Dronacharya, and Karna** the art of war. You do not wing that.

Once prep concludes around the end of 2026, principal photography begins in January 2027 and is expected to run through December. A full calendar year of filming — the kind of timeline that would make a studio accountant flinch but signals the scale **Dinesh Vijan** is chasing. The film was initially announced for a Christmas 2026 release when the first look dropped in November 2024. That date has since been pushed to 2027, a decision that now makes obvious sense given the preparation involved.

And then there is the casting rumour that has Bollywood's attention: **Shraddha Kapoor** is reportedly in advanced talks to play the female lead. According to Mid-Day, the makers approached her as their primary choice, and the pairing — if it materialises — would be a first for both actors. Given Shraddha's box office dominance off **Stree 2** and Vicky's run through **Sam Bahadur** and the upcoming **Love and War**, this would be two of Hindi cinema's most bankable names sharing a frame for the first time. The combination makes commercial sense. It also makes the kind of sense that generates magazine covers.

The first look, released over a year ago, already hinted at the visual ambition. Kaushal was unrecognisable — long hair, a rugged beard, rust-hued dhoti, Rudraksh beads on his wrists, and a weapon in hand. The tagline read: *"The story of Chiranjeevi Parashurama. The Eternal Warrior of Dharma."* It looked like nothing Bollywood had attempted before.

**For diaspora audiences**, Mahavatar represents a particular kind of event film: a Hindu mythological told at Hollywood scale by a director who has proven he can balance spectacle with cultural specificity. Kaushik's Stree films worked because they respected their folklore. If he brings that same sensibility to Parashurama's story — and the eighteen-month window suggests he intends to — this could be the mythological epic Indian cinema has been promising for years.

Vicky Kaushal is betting the most productive stretch of his career on a single character. In an industry addicted to volume, that is either the boldest move of 2026 or the most reckless. The smart money says bold.
